title: Soneva vs Four Seasons Maldives: The Ultimate Luxury Family Resort Showdown
excerpt: Two of the world's most celebrated luxury resort brands go head-to-head for family travelers. We compare Soneva Fushi and Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru across accommodation, kids' clubs, dining, and value to help you choose.
author: Luxury Family Travel Asia Team
content:
The Great Maldives Family Debate

Ask any luxury travel advisor which two resorts dominate family inquiries for the Maldives, and you'll hear the same names: Soneva Fushi and Four Seasons Resort Maldives at Landaa Giraavaru. Both command premium rates. Both have cult-like followings. Both claim to be the ultimate family destination. But they deliver very different experiences. This head-to-head breakdown covers every detail a parent needs to make the right choice for 2026.

Accommodation & Space

Soneva Fushi

Soneva's villas are the largest in the Maldives. The one-bedroom villas start at 375 square metres, and the family-friendly two-bedroom Crusoe Residences span over 600 square metres with private pools, outdoor bathrooms, gardens, and direct beach access. The design is barefoot-luxury: driftwood furniture, outdoor showers, and a 'no news, no shoes' philosophy. Children can run freely between the indoor and outdoor spaces. The sheer sense of space is unmatched.

Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru

The Four Seasons family bungalows and two-bedroom suites are elegant but more restrained at 150–300 square metres. The design is polished Malay-Asian: dark woods, clean lines, and crisp linens. What the Four Seasons lacks in villa size it makes up for in refinement. The Family Beach Bungalow with its plunge pool and direct lagoon access is cleverly configured — parents have privacy while children have their own entrance to the sand.

Winner: Soneva Fushi — The space difference is dramatic, especially for families with young children who need room to play.

Kids' Clubs & Programming

Soneva Fushi

The Den is extraordinary — a dedicated two-story facility with a chef's kitchen where children make their own pizzas, a music room with instruments from around the world, a cinema, and a water-play area. The programming is unstructured and child-led: children choose between glass-blowing sessions (supervised), astronomy in the observatory, or building sandcastles with the Den team. The ratio is exceptional at one staff member per two children. Ages 4–14 welcome.

Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru

Kids for All Seasons is more structured and educational. The marine biology focus sets it apart: children participate in real turtle rehabilitation at the resort's Marine Discovery Centre, plant coral on the house reef, and track manta rays with resident scientists. The Explorer Club for teens (12–17) includes jet-ski tours, sandbank picnics, and DJ workshops. The dedicated teen space with video games and a social calendar means older siblings won't be bored.

Winner: Tie — Soneva wins for unstructured free play; Four Seasons wins for educational content and teen programming. Choose based on your children's ages and interests.

Dining

Soneva Fushi

Soneva has nine dining venues plus in-villa dining. The standout is Fresh in the Garden, an organic garden-to-table experience in the island's vegetable garden. Children can pick their own ingredients. The once-weekly So Starstruck dinner on the sandbank is pure magic. The all-inclusive food-and-beverage package (recommended for families) covers almost everything: premium wines, fresh juices, ice cream from the famous Soneva ice-cream parlour (60 flavours, all complimentary).

Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru

Four venues plus private dining. Blu Beach Club serves exceptional Italian, and Fuego Grill is a family favourite for its interactive teppanyaki. The Al Barakat rooftop Arabic restaurant is a unique offering. The Half Board and Full Board packages are generous but don't cover premium wines or the Japanese restaurant. The children's menu is extensive and well-executed — proper food, not just nuggets.

Winner: Soneva Fushi — The inclusive ice-cream, chocolate room, and garden dining create a more memorable family dining experience.

Service & Butler Experience

Soneva Fushi

Each villa has a Barefoot Guardian — a personal butler who handles everything from unpacking to arranging a beach dinner on 30 minutes' notice. The service is warm and genuinely caring; staff remember children's names and preferences by the second day. The ratio of staff to guests is approximately 5:1.

Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru

Impeccable Four Seasons service with a dedicated Guest Experience Manager for each family. The service is more polished and professional. The concierge team is exceptional at arranging excursions — they'll have a sandbank picnic set up with your children's favourite snacks without being asked. The ratio is approximately 3:1.

Winner: Four Seasons — The polish and proactivity of Four Seasons service edges out Soneva's more relaxed approach for families who appreciate effortless perfection.

Activities & Excursions

Soneva Fushi

The observatory with its resident astronomer is a highlight — children scan Jupiter's moons through a 16-inch telescope. The glass-blowing studio fascinates older kids. Dolphin cruises, snorkeling safaris, and sandbank picnics are all included. The Soul Kitchen provides wellness activities including family yoga and meditation.

Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru

Unparalleled marine biology programme. The turtle rehabilitation centre is genuinely impactful — children can name and track a turtle they help release. Coral planting is a hands-on conservation experience. The manta ray identification programme teaches children about citizen science. The marine biologist-led snorkeling trips are the best in the Maldives for children.

Winner: Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru — The marine biology focus is transformative for children and creates lasting environmental awareness.

Value & Pricing

Both resorts are expensive. Soneva Fushi starts at approximately $2,500/night for a one-bedroom villa in low season, rising to $6,000+ for a two-bedroom Crusoe Residence in peak season. The food-and-beverage inclusive package adds approximately $200/person/night but is worth it for families.

Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru starts at $1,800/night for a Family Beach Bungalow in low season, rising to $4,500+ for a two-bedroom suite in peak. Half Board is included in some packages.

Winner: Four Seasons — Lower entry point and more package flexibility. The marine biology programme is included in the room rate.

The Verdict

Choose Soneva Fushi if: Your children are aged 4–10, you value space above all else, and you want a relaxed barefoot-luxury experience where children can be children without constraint.

Choose Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru if: You have teenagers, your children are passionate about marine life, or you prefer polished service and structured educational programming.

Choose both if: Budget is not a concern and you're staying 10+ nights. Some travel advisors recommend splitting a longer Maldives holiday between the two — a few nights at Soneva for the space and free play, then a few nights at Four Seasons for marine biology and service excellence.

Bottom line: Both are among the world's best family resorts. The choice comes down to your family's age profile and travel style. Either way, your children will experience the Maldives at its finest.
